title: PLA Posts 12 Sorties on May 8 — 10 Cross Median Line Into N/SW/E ADIZ; 6 PLAN Vessels + 2 Official Ships; Continued Elevated Activity 6 Days to Trump-Xi Summit
detail: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense reported 12 PLA aircraft sorties in its daily 06:00 local time snapshot on May 8, 2026, with 10 of 12 sorties crossing the Taiwan Strait median line and entering Taiwan's Air Defense Identification Zone in the northern, southwestern, and eastern sectors. 6 PLAN vessels and 2 official ships continued operating around Taiwan. The May 8 sortie count represents continued elevated activity following the May 7 re-escalation spike (22 sorties, 18 crossing median line) and remains well above the zero-sortie day on May 6, indicating PLA is sustaining meaningful pressure without repeating the dramatic spikes of May 7 and May 2 (29 sorties). The May sortie sequence: 4 (May 1) → 29 new non-exercise record (May 2) → 1 (May 3) → 2 (May 4) → 1 (May 5) → 0 (May 6) → 22 (May 7) → 12 (May 8). With 6 days remaining before the Trump-Xi Beijing summit (May 14-15), PLA's sustained elevated activity frames the diplomatic context as Taiwan's Legislative Yuan passed the NT$780 billion special defense budget the same day. ROC Armed Forces monitored the situation and responded by dispatching combat air patrol aircraft, naval vessels, and coastal missile systems.

media.caption: ANI News: Taiwan detects 12 PLA sorties, 10 crossing median line (N/SW/E ADIZ), 6 PLAN vessels + 2 official ships on May 8 — continued elevated activity 6 days before Trump-Xi summit

title: Taiwan Legislative Yuan Passes NT$780B (US$24.8B) Special Defense Budget — Largest in History; KMT/TPP 59-0 With 48 Abstentions; 6 Days Before Trump-Xi Summit; $14B PAC-3/NASAMS Package Still Pending
detail: Taiwan's Legislative Yuan passed the Special Law for Procuring Defense Equipment (NT$780 billion / ~US$24.8 billion) on May 8, 2026 — the largest defense budget in Taiwan's history — clearing the body 6 days before the May 14-15 Trump-Xi Beijing summit. The bill passed 59-0 with 48 abstentions, driven by the combined KMT-TPP legislative majority. The NT$780 billion figure represents a compromise between the ruling DPP government's NT$1.25 trillion request and the KMT's NT$380 billion and TPP's NT$400 billion alternatives. The final bill is structured in two phases: Phase 1 (NT$300 billion) covers previously US-approved arms from the December 2025 $11.154B package — including 82 HIMARS launchers, M109A7 self-propelled howitzers, Javelin and TOW anti-tank missiles, and anti-armor drone systems; Phase 2 (NT$480 billion) is specifically designated to fund an anticipated second US arms package. The $14 billion PAC-3 MSE / NASAMS package remains on hold and will not be formally announced until after President Trump's Beijing visit. The American Institute in Taiwan emphasized that a 'comprehensive' special budget is crucial for Taiwan's deterrence capability and had actively lobbied for passage. The NT$780B passage came one day after Taiwan became eligible for a floor vote — May 8 was the first permissible date after the 4th cross-party negotiation round collapsed on May 6. The bill runs through 2033 with potential legislative extension. Critics note the NT$780B figure is 37.5% below the full NT$1.25T request and the Phase 2 PAC-3/NASAMS arms remain formally unapproved pending the Trump-Xi summit outcome.

media.caption: Bloomberg: Taiwan passes NT$780 billion (US$24.8B) special defense budget — largest in history; KMT/TPP majority 59-0 with 48 abstentions; Phase 1 HIMARS/howitzers + Phase 2 PAC-3/NASAMS pending

Taipei Times: Legislature passes NT$780bn special arms procurement act — 59-0 with 48 abstentions; DPP-backed government accepts compromise from NT$1.25T request; $14B PAC-3/NASAMS still awaiting Trump-Xi summit
